title: Concord Control Systems Ltd - 543619 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore with PAT INR 42.7 crore and executable order book of about INR 697 crore, 3.3x FY26 revenue.
summary.overview: Management (Joint MD Gaurav Lath) framed Concord as evolving from a railway equipment maker into a full-stack railway technology and lifecycle platform, built on four pillars: green mobility, smart locomotive intelligence, railway safety (Kavach/MSDAC), and AI-driven diagnostics. FY26 figures stated were revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore, PAT INR 42.7 crore, EBITDA INR 62.1 crore, and an executable order book of about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026. Working capital was the main analyst concern: receivables and short-term debt rose sharply, which management attributed to back-ended railway billing in Q4 and said will persist through the growth phase. Several questions on Fusion Electronics revenue, Kavach tender outcomes and loco-Kavach opportunity size got non-committal answers.

financial_highlights.change: about 3.3x FY26 revenue; prior-year order book cited by analyst as INR 212 crore

financial_highlights.value: around 30% (as cited by analyst, not disputed by management)
40% to 50% CAGR (as cited in analyst question)

segments.name: Fusion Electronics (flex PCB / premium EMS subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Acquired last year; management called it a turnaround with no meaningful revenue yet. At full scale it can do about INR 200 crore revenue on installed capacity, with capacity doubling planned. Management expects the first revenue-contributing year in the current year.

segments.name: Locomotive solutions
segments.commentary: Management said locomotive solutions are currently the larger contributor to growth, including DPWCS (distributed power wireless control systems). No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota)
segments.commentary: Field trials started; management hopes for a successful year. Trial completion and ISA approval are targeted within FY27. Kavach pillar is positioned as large and long-duration, with no revenue figure given.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Demonstrated India's first indigenous zero-emission diesel-to-battery locomotive retrofit. Also cited a recent NTPC order, with no value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40% to 50% CAGR going forward, as cited by analyst; management did not dispute it.
EBITDA margin guidance of 20% to 25%; management said guidance is realistic, not conservative.
Typical order execution cycle of 18 to 24 months per management.
Fusion Electronics expected to contribute revenue in the current financial year; no figure given.
Management aims to complete Kavach trial and ISA approvals within FY27, with geopolitical factors cited as a constraint.
Management did not give a peak debt or working capital estimate; said Q1 receivables will be high and working capital needs will persist.
capex_capacity: Fusion Electronics has installed flex PCB and box-build capacity; full-scale revenue potential about INR 200 crore with capacity doubling provision.
Management said it has been frugal on investment and will consider raising its Progota stake when returns justify it; no decision announced.
Field-level in-house engineering team on locomotives reportedly gives execution efficiency for loco Kavach installation.
demand_pricing: Executable order book about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026, about 3.3x FY26 revenue.
Management described an unprecedented order book; no split by product or customer was given.
Kavach: a tender for about 4,500 loco units closed 14 April 2026 with no outcome yet. Management said tender finalisation takes time and Concord has quoted several tenders.
Management did not confirm the analyst's figure of about 17,000 loco units tendered; it said the total loco population is 13,000 to 16,000 including train sets and MEMUs.
No direct response on whether the LNG and geopolitical crisis could slow railway spending, beyond general references to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise sharply, and will this working capital pattern continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to back-ended Q4 billing and customer acceptance cycles with railways. Said receivable cycles had improved by June versus last year, and confirmed similar working capital will recur.

qa_highlights.question: How should debt and balance sheet strength be seen over the next few years, given short-term debt rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is always heavier and working capital will spike with the INR 697 crore order book, then ease. It declined to give peak debt estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% to 25% EBITDA guidance conservative given around 30% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for realistic guidance and that technology adoption is faster than expected, without accepting the conservatism framing.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and is there any liquidity challenge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said railway payments are streamlined and sovereign-backed with no penalty or bad-debt risk, and that cash flow will not deter growth. Confirmed that some money started coming in from April, but gave no timeline for positive operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company face penalties for delayed order execution, and will it grow execution faster than 40% to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company executed similar growth last year and planned more structured execution for the large order book. No penalty figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can Fusion Electronics deliver this year, and why has it shown little revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a turnaround with a typical 300-day integration cycle and said full-scale revenue could be about INR 200 crore. It expects revenue contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will Kavach orders be executed, and when will the 4,500-unit loco Kavach tender be decided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kavach orders have two to three phases (production, inspection, installation), with part of the invoice paid on delivery and the balance after installation. The tender outcome timing was not given; it said finalisation is a process.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: receivables and short-term debt rose sharply; no peak debt or cash-flow-positive timeline was given.
Fusion Electronics has not yet shown meaningful revenue; the turnaround timeline is open-ended.
Kavach tender (about 4,500 loco units, closed 14 April 2026) outcome is pending; trial completion and ISA approvals depend on geopolitical factors.
Execution risk on a INR 697 crore order book with an 18 to 24 month cycle and possible penalties for delays (not addressed in detail).
Mainboard migration timeline was not given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on strategy and long-term platform vision, with repeated emphasis on railway payments being sovereign-backed. Evasive on specifics: Fusion revenue, Kavach tender timing, loco count, peak debt and mainboard timing all received non-committal answers.
key_quotes: Concord is no longer just a railway equipment manufacturer.
This order book is more than three times of our FY26 revenue, giving us a very strong visibility and confidence.
There is absolutely no issue in railway payments.
We are overly cautious in saving each penny and maintaining our cash flows.

adds.what: Fusion Electronics flex PCB and box-build capacity doubling (provision; no capex or timing given)

growth.why: Analyst-cited 40-50% CAGR guidance was not disputed and is backed by a INR 697 crore executable order book (about 3.3x FY26 revenue) with 18-24 month execution cycles, but no capacity additions with figures or timing were given and Fusion Electronics revenue timing is only 'hoped' for this year.
